title: 83. Numeracy & Number Systems: Rounding to a Fixed Number of Decimal Places
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.learningObjective: Round a decimal directly to the specified number of decimal places, including any necessary carries.
questions.question: Round \(3.47\) to \(1\) decimal place. Use round-to-nearest with exact halfway cases rounded upward.
questions.explanation: To round to \(1\) decimal place, look at the digit in the hundredths place. In \(3.47\), the hundredths digit is \(7\). Since \(7 \ge 5\), increase the tenths digit \(4\) by \(1\), giving \(3.5\). Therefore, \(3.47\) rounded to \(1\) decimal place is \(3.5\). The alternative truncates without applying the rounding test.
questions.hint: Check the digit immediately to the right of the required decimal place.

questions.learningObjective: Round a decimal directly to the specified number of decimal places, including any necessary carries.
questions.question: Round \(12.348\) to \(2\) decimal places. Use round-to-nearest with exact halfway cases rounded upward.
questions.explanation: To round to \(2\) decimal places, look at the digit in the thousandths place. In \(12.348\), the thousandths digit is \(8\). Since \(8 \ge 5\), increase the hundredths digit \(4\) by \(1\), giving \(12.35\). Therefore, \(12.348\) rounded to \(2\) decimal places is \(12.35\). The alternative truncates without applying the rounding test.
questions.hint: The third digit after the decimal point decides whether to round up or keep the second digit.

questions.concept: Rounding a Decimal Less Than One
questions.learningObjective: Round a decimal directly to the specified number of decimal places, including any necessary carries.
questions.question: Round \(0.876\) to \(2\) decimal places. Use round-to-nearest with exact halfway cases rounded upward.
questions.explanation: To round \(0.876\) to \(2\) decimal places, look at the thousandths digit, which is \(6\). Since \(6 \ge 5\), increase the hundredths digit \(7\) by \(1\), giving \(0.88\). Therefore, \(0.876\) rounded to \(2\) decimal places is \(0.88\). The alternative ignores the deciding digit.
questions.hint: Round up when the digit after the required place is \(5\) or greater.

questions.learningObjective: Round a decimal directly to the specified number of decimal places, including any necessary carries.
questions.question: Round \(5.995\) to \(2\) decimal places. Use round-to-nearest with exact halfway cases rounded upward.
questions.explanation: To round \(5.995\) to \(2\) decimal places, look at the thousandths digit, which is \(5\). Since \(5 \ge 5\), increase the hundredths digit \(9\) by \(1\). This causes a carry through the tenths place, so \(5.995\) becomes \(6.00\). Therefore, \(5.995\) rounded to \(2\) decimal places is \(6.00\). The alternative \(5.99\) simply drops the thousandths digit without rounding up, so the stated halfway rule is never applied.
questions.hint: First find the digit immediately after the required decimal place and decide whether to round up; if you do, check what happens to the digit you increase.

questions.learningObjective: Round a decimal directly to the specified number of decimal places, including any necessary carries.
questions.question: Round \(8.1349\) to \(3\) decimal places. Use round-to-nearest with exact halfway cases rounded upward.
questions.explanation: To round \(8.1349\) to \(3\) decimal places, look at the fourth decimal digit, which is \(9\). Since \(9 \ge 5\), increase the third decimal digit \(4\) by \(1\), giving \(8.135\). Therefore, \(8.1349\) rounded to \(3\) decimal places is \(8.135\). The alternative truncates without applying the rounding test.
questions.hint: The fourth digit after the decimal point determines the rounding of the third digit.

questions.concept: Rounding That Produces a Whole Number
questions.learningObjective: Round a decimal directly to the specified number of decimal places, including any necessary carries.
questions.question: Round \(0.9995\) to \(3\) decimal places. Use round-to-nearest with exact halfway cases rounded upward.
questions.explanation: To round \(0.9995\) to \(3\) decimal places, look at the fourth decimal digit, which is \(5\). Since \(5 \ge 5\), increase the third decimal digit \(9\) by \(1\). This carry makes all three decimal digits zero and increases the whole-number part to \(1\), so the result is \(1.000\). Therefore, \(0.9995\) rounded to \(3\) decimal places is \(1.000\). The alternative \(0.999\) simply drops the fourth decimal digit without rounding up, so the stated halfway rule is never applied.
questions.hint: First find the digit immediately after the required decimal place and decide whether to round up; if you do, check what happens to the digit you increase.

questions.concept: Rounding to One Decimal Place with Carry
questions.learningObjective: Round a decimal directly to the specified number of decimal places, including any necessary carries.
questions.question: Round \(2.96\) to \(1\) decimal place. Use round-to-nearest with exact halfway cases rounded upward.
questions.explanation: To round \(2.96\) to \(1\) decimal place, look at the hundredths digit, which is \(6\). Since \(6 \ge 5\), increase the tenths digit \(9\) by \(1\). This carry changes \(2.96\) to \(3.0\). Therefore, \(2.96\) rounded to \(1\) decimal place is \(3.0\). The alternative \(2.9\) simply drops the hundredths digit without rounding up, although \(6 \ge 5\).
questions.hint: First find the digit immediately after the required decimal place and decide whether to round up; if you do, check what happens to the digit you increase.

questions.concept: Rounding a Number Just Below a Whole Number
questions.learningObjective: Round a decimal directly to the specified number of decimal places, including any necessary carries.
questions.question: Round \(47.999\) to \(2\) decimal places. Use round-to-nearest with exact halfway cases rounded upward.
questions.explanation: To round \(47.999\) to \(2\) decimal places, look at the third decimal digit, which is \(9\). Since \(9 \ge 5\), increase the hundredths digit \(9\) by \(1\). This causes a carry through the tenths and units places, giving \(48.00\). Therefore, \(47.999\) rounded to \(2\) decimal places is \(48.00\). The alternative \(47.99\) simply drops the third decimal digit without rounding up, although \(9 \ge 5\).
questions.hint: First find the digit immediately after the required decimal place and decide whether to round up; if you do, check what happens to the digit you increase.

questions.concept: Rounding a Small Decimal with Leading Zeros
questions.learningObjective: Round a decimal directly to the specified number of decimal places, including any necessary carries.
questions.question: Round \(0.0549\) to \(2\) decimal places. Use round-to-nearest with exact halfway cases rounded upward.
questions.explanation: To round \(0.0549\) to \(2\) decimal places, look at the third decimal digit, which is \(4\). Since \(4 < 5\), keep the hundredths digit \(5\) unchanged and drop the remaining digits. Therefore, \(0.0549\) rounded to \(2\) decimal places is \(0.05\). Rounding first to \(0.055\) and then to \(0.06\) introduces a double-rounding error. Round directly from the original value to the requested precision.
questions.hint: Pay attention to the digit in the thousandths place, even when the number is less than \(0.1\).

questions.concept: Rounding a Number with More Than Three Decimal Places
questions.learningObjective: Round a decimal directly to the specified number of decimal places, including any necessary carries.
questions.question: Round \(123.4567\) to \(3\) decimal places. Use round-to-nearest with exact halfway cases rounded upward.
questions.explanation: To round \(123.4567\) to \(3\) decimal places, look at the fourth decimal digit, which is \(7\). Since \(7 \ge 5\), increase the third decimal digit \(6\) by \(1\), giving \(123.457\). Therefore, \(123.4567\) rounded to \(3\) decimal places is \(123.457\). The alternative truncates without applying the rounding test.
questions.hint: Use the fourth digit after the decimal point to decide how to round the third digit.
